## 15. Repository and pins design

**Layout.** The repository is `ChristopherLinnett/craftbridge` (MIT OR Apache-2.0; private until hosted CI starts, then public, PD3), checked out at `artcraft-plugin-port/` (PD16). It has one folder per platform, each a complete build, and nothing of a platform at its root (PD19). A toolchain's build files sit only in its own platform folder: no `Cargo.toml`, `Package.swift` or Gradle build or settings file stands anywhere else — a cross-platform folder, another platform's folder or the plan, bar the probes kept under `plan/evidence/` — where no build would read it (AGENTS §1). Inside each platform folder the universal core sits beside the app plugin (PD10), and samples sit beside the library they consume (D-1).

**Dependency direction.** Within the core and within a plugin, dependencies point down the layers. `rust/xtask/src/layers.rs` lists each crate's layer once, and the gate fails on any edge the table does not allow (D-25).

| Layer | Crate | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| core 0 | `craftbridge-media` | external crates; `filmcraft-codecs`, `filmcraft-color`, `filmcraft-frame` and `filmcraft-isobmff` at EffectCraft's FilmCraft revision (PD18) |
| core 1 | `craftbridge-core` | a lower core rank |
| core 2 | `craftbridge-core-ffi` | the lower core ranks; `uniffi` |
| app 0 | `craftbridge-effects` | any core crate; `effectcraft-*` |
| app 1 | `craftbridge-effects-ffi` | a lower rank of its app, and any core crate; `uniffi` |
| tool | `craftbridge-effects-codegen`, `craftbridge-effects-conformance`, `uniffi-bindgen`, `xtask` | anything; nothing depends on a tool |
| support | `craftbridge-process` | external crates that are no Craft app's; no CraftBridge crate. A tool depends on it; a core or app crate only from its tests |

Every row may also take external crates that are no Craft app's.

- A core crate never depends on an `effectcraft-*` crate or on an app crate, not even in its tests (PD9). An app crate never depends on another app's crates, not even in its tests: code two plugins need moves into the core (PD18). The rank and `uniffi` rules are about what ships, so dev-dependencies, which only a crate's own tests compile, are outside them; the tool rule is not, since a tool may reach every app, and a test that took one would reach them through it. The support crate is host code the tools share (starting a process in a group of its own and stopping the whole group, so a timed-out step leaves nothing of its group running, and running one ignored test of the current test binary again in a child started with a changed environment): a tool may depend on it, a core or app crate only from its tests, and it depends on no CraftBridge crate and no Craft app's crate, even from its own tests. A Craft app's crate is known by its name or by the app's repository it comes from.
- `uniffi` appears only in `-ffi` crates, and only an app's `-ffi` crate builds a `staticlib` or `cdylib`, and it builds both; no crate is a Rust `dylib` (D-4).
- Every crate is a workspace member in the folder its row gives it (`core/<name>`, `<app>/<name>`, or `<name>` for a tool that is no app's and for the support crate), its library and binaries named after it, and a core crate's name carries none of the Craft apps' nouns, because the core serves them all; a dependency by a path outside the workspace, or on a workspace crate's name from anywhere else, is refused, and so is every local package of the resolved graph, every feature on, that is no member (a path, `[patch]` or `[replace]` brings it in), and every `Cargo.toml` under `rust/` but the workspace's, its members' and the gate's lint library's, `rust/never-crash-lints/Cargo.toml`, which `cargo dylint` builds in the stages that run it (Gate machinery, below).
- Swift: `CraftBridgeFFI` ← `CraftBridge` ← `CraftBridgeEffects`. Kotlin: `:effects` exposes `:core`. Swift and Kotlin take the same rule as Rust: a plugin target or plugin module depends only on the core (in Swift, the core's targets `CraftBridge`, the generated `CraftBridgeFFI` and its binary target), `CraftBridge` and `:core` depend on no plugin, and no plugin depends on another; the package manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`, and Gradle's own project graph, declared and resolved, enforce this. A platform folder never refers to another platform's code; every platform reads `conformance/`.
- Code and data a generator in this repository writes live only in `generated` or `Generated` directories, carry an `@generated` header where the format has comments (in Markdown, an HTML comment; JSON, CSV, plain text and binary files need none), are committed, and are written only by `cargo xtask generate` (D-26, L10); a marker anywhere else, the root's own files included, is a generated file in the wrong place. Three kinds of written-for-you file are outside that rule: what a build tool writes for itself (`Cargo.lock`, `Package.resolved`, the Gradle wrapper), which change only through that tool; the `[patch.crates-io]`, `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.release]` tables of `rust/Cargo.toml` and the starting `Cargo.lock`, which only `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes from the pinned EffectCraft (Pins, below); and the plan's views in `plan/`, which the plan kit builds from this file and `plan/diagrams/src/`: the gate's Plan stage rebuilds those views from their sources and fails on any byte that differs, bar the drawing in each diagram's SVG export, which only draw.io Desktop writes (the gate, below), and `plan/plan check --final` checks this file against the plan's own writing rules and reports a view older than what builds it.

**Pins.** `[workspace.dependencies]` names each EffectCraft crate CraftBridge uses (`effectcraft-engine`, `-host`, `-automation`, `-gpu`, `-render`, `-time`, `-text`, `-media`, `-expr`, `-script`, `-plugin`, `-raster`) with `git = "https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft"` and one `rev`, an official revision (`10376058` at the start, PD4, PD17), and `filmcraft-codecs`, `filmcraft-color`, `filmcraft-frame` and `filmcraft-isobmff` with EffectCraft's own FilmCraft revision `d5ead4ba` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:89-90`), so CraftBridge's decoders register into the same registry EffectCraft decodes through (D-13). Those are the crates `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes, so the `upstream` rule refuses any other EffectCraft or FilmCraft crate pinned there, which would keep its revision when the pin moves.

- Cargo applies `[patch]` tables and profiles only at the root workspace, so EffectCraft's own `[patch.crates-io]` entries (`hayro-syntax`, `hayro-jbig2` and the egui family, `effectcraft: Cargo.toml:223-239`), its `[profile.release]` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:219-221`) and its `[profile.dev]` (`effectcraft: Cargo.toml:149-217`: `opt-level = 2` for every dependency, 1 for the workspace's own crates, 3 for the pixel and codec crates, each with upstream's comment, but not its `dev-full` debugger profile) are **generated** into `rust/Cargo.toml` from the pinned upstream `Cargo.toml` by `tools/update-upstream.sh`, and `Cargo.lock` starts from the pinned upstream `Cargo.lock`. No line of them is written by hand (D-21). The dev profile makes every test run EffectCraft's and FilmCraft's code optimised, as EffectCraft's own tests do; it leaves CraftBridge's own crates their debug assertions and overflow checks, which the gate holds every build of tests to in every unit of theirs it compiles — the tests, the libraries they link, and the build scripts and proc-macros that make what they run — from Cargo's own report of the profile it built each unit in (`cargo xtask compiled`).
- Nothing in EffectCraft is changed, and CraftBridge never builds from a fork or a patched branch; the fork `ChristopherLinnett/effectcraft` is only kept in step with upstream (PD17).

**The adaptations** (PD5, D-29). Where a phone needs EffectCraft to do something differently, CraftBridge does it in its own crates on EffectCraft's public interfaces, never by copying EffectCraft code. `tools/adaptations.toml` lists each adaptation with the EffectCraft files and items it relies on, so the update script names the adaptations an update touches (§24). An adaptation that mirrors what the command line does lists, among the items it relies on, the command line's own code it mirrors, each place whole code that neither stops inside a block nor runs past one, so any change to that code, a line added inside a block of it included, names the adaptation as any other item does. An adaptation upstream made needless does not leave the list: its entry stays, marked `retired` with the id of the upstream commit whose interface replaced it and with its items removed, so its id holds its place in the order and is never reused; the reader checks a retired entry's id with the others, and that it names that commit and holds no items, and reads nothing else of it, and the update's report lists retired entries apart from the live ones (AGENTS §7).

| AD8 | `craftbridge-media` registers its hardware decoder factory in FilmCraft's decoder registry, sets FilmCraft's hardware-decoding switch, and wraps each hardware decoder in `Fallback`, which follows `HybridDecoder`'s behaviour in its own code: on an error, an in-band parameter change or a failure while the stream's end is drained (FilmCraft's `VideoDecoder::flush` answers no result, so the hardware decoder answers a drain's error through CraftBridge's own `Draining`) it switches to FilmCraft's software decoder and replays from a restart sample before the oldest picture the caller does not have yet — departing from `HybridDecoder`, whose start moves as each restart sample arrives (to it, or after an HEVC CRA to the one before) and which takes the pictures the failed decoder still held from its flush, because a MediaCodec codec loses the pictures it holds when it fails and a start moved on arrival would leave their samples out of the replay; the start moves to a restart sample once the caller has the picture of every sample before it, and to a CRA only once the caller has the CRA's own picture, since pictures come out in presentation order and the CRA's leading pictures, which a replay from it leaves out, come out before it; **States.**
- *Pinned*: `rev` names an official storytold/effectcraft commit; `info` reports that commit in full as `pin` (§21).
- *Update in progress*: the update script has moved the pin and named the adaptations whose EffectCraft code changed; the update merges once each named adaptation is rechecked and the gate passes (§24).

**Edge cases.**
- An update changes code an adaptation follows (a new `render` flag, a renamed command an adaptation calls): the script names the adaptation; `RenderRequest` gains the field and the corpus the scenario, in the same update.
- An update removes a public item an adaptation uses: the build fails at the gate, and the adaptation is rewritten on what upstream offers instead, in the same update.
- Upstream adds a public interface that does what an adaptation does (a session with explicit folders, an encoder interface): the adaptation moves onto it and its entry in `tools/adaptations.toml` is retired (upstream wins, AGENTS §7).

**The gate.** `tools/ci.sh` is the one entry point for people, agents and CI (D-25). Before any stage it refuses a Rust toolchain other than the one `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` pins, any rustup override of `rust/`, the same in the lint library's folder against the nightly its own `rust-toolchain.toml` pins, and an environment that switches what the Rust tools check (a rustflags or rustdocflags variable, a compiler, wrapper, rustdoc or rustfmt, a runner or linker, a profile or alias override, another lockfile, `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP`, `CLIPPY_CONF_DIR`, dylint's `DYLINT_*`), naming the variable — and the same switches written as keys in any Cargo configuration Cargo reads for a build in `rust/` are refused the same way: one table, `tools/refused-switches.tsv`, names every switch by its configuration key and the variables Cargo derives from it, the environment check and the rules' key check read that one table, and the rules name the file and the key — and reads the pins of both pin files through `cargo xtask pins`, from an xtask it built in that run. It runs `tools/doctor.sh --gate`, then the rules, which need no build, before any stage compiles the workspace (so no build script runs before the gate has judged whether it may exist), then every other stage, and one run reports every failure; `tools/ci.sh <stage or group>…` runs only those named, every name checked before the first runs.

|---|---|
| Rust | `cargo fmt --check`, of the lint library too; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -D warnings` of what ships, and of the tests with the two calls-by-path lints taken back; the never-crash calls and the ways to stop the process also named by path in `rust/clippy.toml` (`disallowed-methods`, `disallowed-macros`), which reach a macro's expansion, a method taken as a value, and an exit in a method or a `main`, which clippy's `exit` passes, and indexing's own trait methods, `core::ops::Index::index` and `core::ops::IndexMut::index_mut`, so an index spelled as a call — `d.index(i)`, `(Index::index)(d, i)`, a captured `C::index` — falls to the same rule whatever it indexes, and `std::env::args` and `std::env::vars`, which panic on an item that is not Unicode, so code reads `args_os` and `vars_os`; the `[]` clippy's index lints do not read — on a map, a `VecDeque` or anything with an `Index` of its own, which clippy reads only held by value with a `get` that returns what the index yields — refused by `collection_indexing`, a `forbid` lint of the gate's lint library `rust/never-crash-lints` wherever the workspace writes it, its own macros' expansions included (there a slice's and a string's `[]` too, which clippy's index lints do not read inside another crate's macro) and std's and dependencies' not, which `cargo dylint`, at the release `tools/env.sh` pins, builds with the nightly the library's own `rust-toolchain.toml` pins and runs over the same shipping targets, and over the library builds of the phone runs in the mobile stage, every other stage building the workspace with its own toolchain, and `cargo test -p xtask` running the library over a probe crate, so a library that compiles and lints nothing fails the test stage, and it and clippy over one probe, so each index is reported once (AGENTS §3, decision #153), and clippy over the library's own code on that nightly in the workspace's two runs, failing on any warning, with the library's own lint over what it ships, under the copy of the workspace's lint table its own manifest carries, beside the workspace's edition and licence, which xtask's tests keep identical to the originals and its crate inherits as a member does, the rules reading its manifest, graph and compilation as a member's (AGENTS §3); every file each of these compilations reads, from the compiler's dep-info (`cargo xtask compiled`), one of its crate's own `.rs` files the rules read (or the lint library its runs load), so no `#[path]`, `include!` or `include_str!` reaches another; `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` over every feature, and over the lint library's own dependencies; no cargo stage runs while the repository root holds a `.cargo` folder |
| Rules | `cargo xtask rules`: one reading of every file (text UTF-8 with no NUL, paths in NFC, known names and endings spelt the canonical way, no symbolic link, no Rust, Swift, Kotlin or shell outside the code folders but `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/`); no absolute home-folder path (`/Users/<name>/`, `/home/<name>/`, in any case) in a file git tracks, read by `git grep` over the work tree and named by file and line, since the repository is public; the root and platform-folder layout, with no `node_modules` in the code folders, no hand-written Java under `android/sdk` (whose never-crash and JNI rules are written for Kotlin alone), and no platform build file — a `Cargo.toml`, a `Package.swift`, a Gradle build or settings file — anywhere the repository holds it but its own platform folder and the plan's evidence; layers and dependency direction over the resolved graph with every feature, no local package outside the workspace however it is brought in, in Swift too (the manifest, read by `swift package dump-package`, which needs no native library built), with no plugin depending on a plugin; the inherited lint table, its no-exception lints `forbid` — among them `exit`, `indexing_slicing` and `string_slice`, which refuse stopping the process and an unchecked index into a slice, array, vector or string — weakened by no crate, module, item (bar `expect_used`'s literal), clippy configuration, Cargo configuration, target runner or compiler wrapper, with a build script (as `cargo metadata` reports it) only for a crate the layer table marks, every crate inheriting the workspace edition with `edition.workspace = true`, no target table writing an edition of its own, and `cargo metadata`'s resolved edition, the crate's and each of its targets', the workspace's, and `panic = "unwind"`; `unsafe` only in a platform crate's own `src/platform/` (D-20), read from Rust's syntax tree by `syn` (D-28); generated-file placement; one copy of each gate configuration, and none of the tool configurations that would switch a check off (Gate machinery, below); the licences of what the builds use — every external module resolved onto a Gradle library module's release, unit-test and instrumented-test runtime classpaths, or onto the tool classpaths of the detekt the gate runs its Kotlin checks with (the rule project's compile, runtime and test classpaths, and the analyser's own), every package a `Package.swift` names (as `swift package dump-package` reads it) and every pin a `Package.resolved` records, committed whenever the package takes a published one, each declared in `tools/licences.toml`, with build plugins checked by name from the catalog's `[plugins]`; one copy of each EffectCraft, FilmCraft and Craft library crate (D-13), bar a Craft library crate the pinned EffectCraft's own lock already resolves at two official revisions, held to exactly that split; the EffectCraft pin a commit official main reaches, named by its id, the generated tables exactly what `tools/update-upstream.sh` writes, every EffectCraft, FilmCraft and Craft library package of `Cargo.lock` from a source the pin sanctions, down to the commit Cargo builds, and no Cargo configuration Cargo reads for a build in `rust/` — the repository's own, those in every folder above the checkout, the cargo home's, whatever those `include`, and the environment the gate runs in — holds a `[patch]`, `paths` or a `[source]` replacement, nor a refused switch written as a key: the one table `tools/refused-switches.tsv` names every refused switch by its configuration key and the variables Cargo derives from it — rustflags and rustdocflags, a compiler and its wrappers, rustdoc, runners, linkers, a dependency's build-script override and every other target key, profiles, aliases, the build target, another lockfile than the committed one, and every `[env]` entry — and the committed `rust/.cargo/config.toml` may set only what it holds today: the `xtask` alias, and only while it still runs the xtask package; the file and key are named for each, and because both the environment check and the key check read that one table, neither can drift from the other (Pins) |
| Generated | `cargo xtask generate --check`: everything regenerated, any difference fails, and so does a file there git does not track (L10) |
| Plan | `cargo xtask plan-views --check`: the plan kit's own builders, `build/build-diagrams.mjs` then `build/build-plan.mjs` as `plan/package.json` names them, rebuild every view from this file and `plan/diagrams/src/` into a scratch copy of the plan's files (git's, so the ignore files alone say what is no part of the plan), and any byte that differs fails, named — so a view edited by hand fails here whatever its time says, and no list of the views is kept to fall out of date. It runs on Node and `npm ci` in `plan/` and nothing else: `--no-shots` keeps a browser down (this plan builds no mockup gallery), and the diagram build runs with the absolute path of `true` as draw.io's exporter (`DRAWIO_BIN`, which the kit passes over for draw.io Desktop when it names no file the kit can find), so each `.drawio` and the kit's trimming of each SVG export are weighed and no app starts; an export in the diagrams' folder that no source builds any more fails too, since nothing would rebuild it again. The drawing in each SVG export is the one thing it cannot weigh: it is draw.io Desktop's own rendering, holding no copy of the diagram, and no version here pins that app; a hand edit to one still fails through the HTML, which inlines it, until the HTML is rebuilt, and `plan/plan check --final` reports an export older than its source |
| Swift | `swift format lint --strict` (`cargo xtask swift-format`) on every Swift file the rules' walk lists, whose never-crash rules (force unwraps and `as!`, `try!`, implicitly unwrapped optionals) neither its configuration nor a file-wide `swift-format-ignore-file` switches off, and whose own test exemption reaches only the files SwiftPM compiles into its test targets (`swift package describe`): `import XCTest` is refused everywhere and Swift Testing outside a test target; UniFFI's generated bindings (`ios/sdk/Sources/CraftBridgeFFI/Platform/Generated/`, §20), whose templates are fixed, are linted with the same configuration and only the rules those templates cannot meet switched off, each named with its reason in `rust/xtask/src/swift_format.rs`; `cargo xtask swift-lint`: SwiftLint's built-in `missing_docs` on every `open` and `public` declaration, protocol requirements and enum cases included, and the rest read through SourceKit-LSP with SwiftPM's settings for every build of the package that ships — Debug and Release for each Apple slice `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` builds the native library for, the iOS device and the iOS Simulator — so each `#if` branch a shipping build compiles is read resolved and the compiler's own tokens, symbols and declarations say what a name means: neither a Swift 6 regex literal nor a comment hides code and no plain-text scan is left to be fooled (SwiftLint's custom rules lex Swift 5, where `/\/*/` opens a comment): outside test targets the never-crash calls (`fatalError`, `exit`, `abort` and the like, called or taken as a value, however qualified) unless they resolve to a declaration of ours, every postfix `!` and `.unsafelyUnwrapped`; in tests too the pointer APIs, a pointer type reached through a type alias (ours or the SDK's) and a binding to a C symbol confined to `Platform/`; everywhere a `swiftlint:` command, and a swift-format ignore that switches a never-crash rule off file-wide, switches every rule off, reaches beyond one function or property, or gives no reason (D-28); the generated bindings' folder alone exempt from `missing_docs`, `fatalError` and the postfix `!`, which UniFFI's templates cannot meet, each named with its reason in `rust/xtask/src/swift_lint.rs`, and every other rule, the pointer confinement included, holding there; and, from the same resolved package (`swift package describe`, which describes no package whose native library is not built), every regular target at `Sources/<name>`, moved by no `path:` and found in no other source folder, and every Swift target built and compiling only files the checks read; every target, test targets included (`build build-for-testing`), built in Debug and in Release for each Apple slice `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` names, the iOS device and the iOS Simulator, as `cargo xtask swift-builds` lists them from the table the Swift checks read (the lint refuses a regular target no product and no test target uses, which the scheme would not build), with an import the package does not declare an error (`DIAGNOSE_MISSING_TARGET_DEPENDENCIES=YES_ERROR`), so `CraftBridge` cannot import a plugin |
| Android | Spotless (ktlint, from the root `.editorconfig` alone, run every time and never replayed from a cache, in a Gradle build of its own: ktlint sets and puts back IntelliJ's JVM-wide path settings as it starts, which crashes a Lint starting in the same JVM), detekt for the never-crash calls, the JNI declarations confined to `platform/` in every source set, the package every module's own files and its generated bindings declare, and the refusal of a suppression written over a whole file, switching a gate rule off on an item, or of a compiler error anywhere but the generated bindings (which the compiler's analysis names), read from Kotlin's own syntax tree with its types resolved (D-28), Android Lint on the debug and the release variant, the release build and the unit-test and instrumented-test Kotlin compilations, with warnings as errors, and explicit API mode on the library code (Kotlin exempts tests from it, and Lint runs only its test checks there), and each module's unit tests, run on the TestNG `build-logic` gives every module; the build itself refuses a module that skips the convention plugin or sets its rules back, a check the gate asks for that no longer brings the tasks doing its work, a project dependency, declared or resolved, from `:core` on any module or from a plugin module on anything but `:core`, and a Kotlin or Java file under a module's `src` in no source folder of the compilations AGP builds for it (`src/testRelease/kotlin`, which AGP 9 compiles for no library), which would be formatted and never compiled (AGENTS §3); a task any module disables or skips with `onlyIf` reports SKIPPED, which `cargo xtask skipped-tasks` reads from Gradle's log and fails the stage on |
| Shell | `shellcheck --norc` on every script the rules' walk lists, told by its `.sh` ending or a `#!` line naming sh, bash, dash or ksh, bar the Gradle wrapper, which Gradle writes; `plan/` holds no script but the plan kit's `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/` |
| Duplicates | jscpd over Rust, Swift, Kotlin and shell: a block of ten lines, or of seventy tokens, repeated anywhere fails, in two passes because jscpd applies its two minimums together; jscpd reads the rules' own file list, which leaves out generated directories and build output and nothing else (`plan/` holds none of the four languages but `plan/plan` and the probes kept in `plan/evidence/`), with every script the shell stage checks named to it as bash; jscpd runs with `--no-gitignore`, and the rules refuse the `.ignore` files, nested `.gitignore` files and ignore markers it would honour |
| Conformance | `tools/oracle.sh` builds the official EffectCraft command line at the full commit the pin names, which `cargo xtask upstream source` holds to official main through the upstream cache as the `upstream` rule does (so the pin is written once and the oracle is the commit the workspace builds), and `craftbridge-effects-conformance` runs the desktop corpus (§28) on it and on the plug-in, each as a process in the one cleared environment that holds only its own configuration folder, so no setting of the shell running the gate changes what either renders: the values each scenario names in each side's JSON, the two sides' documents, files byte for byte or within the compositor's own GPU tolerance, and an encoded export frame by frame within D-12's 40 dB PSNR; a failing scenario is named. Both decide what the stage checks, so both are gate machinery (below). After the Rust tests, as a stage of its own, since the oracle is an EffectCraft build (minutes cold, a second warm) |

`cargo xtask rules` reads Rust on the language's own syntax tree, parsed with `syn` (D-28): `unsafe` is found as `syn` finds it (blocks, functions, impls, traits, extern blocks, modules, function-pointer types and attributes), and every lint attribute wherever `syn` finds one (a crate root, a module, an item, an expression, a `cfg_attr`), with a macro's body read as the tokens it is, so an `allow` a macro writes onto a module, or onto whatever item its caller hands it, or one written in the tokens a call hands a macro (which may take them apart and put them together elsewhere), is module-level, an attribute whose level or whole text a macro fills in, or makes of a `#` and brackets it is given apart, is any level, and an attribute name spelt as a raw identifier (`r#allow`) is the attribute the compiler reads. The lint-attribute rule refuses `allow`, `expect` or `warn` of a default clippy group or of `warnings` wherever it sits, and `rustfmt::skip` on a crate root or a module, `cfg_attr(test, …)` aside. A file `syn` cannot parse, or one nested deeper than it reads, fails the check, naming it. No source stripper exists: the Gradle build files' grammar allows one comment form, a whole line starting with `//`, so reading them needs none, and Swift and Kotlin are read by SwiftLint and detekt.

**Gate machinery.** The gate's own machinery decides what the gate checks, so it cannot guard itself: `tools/ci.sh`, `tools/env.sh`, `tools/refused-switches.tsv`, `tools/oracle.sh`, `tools/ios-device-test.sh`, `tools/device-tests.tsv`, `tools/build-xcframework.sh`, `tools/build-android.sh`, `tools/hooks/`, `rust/xtask/`, `rust/never-crash-lints/`, `rust/effects/craftbridge-effects-conformance/`, `rust/craftbridge-process/`, `rust/.cargo/config.toml`, `android/sdk/settings.gradle.kts`, `android/sdk/gradle.properties`, `android/sdk/build-logic/`, and the single copy of each of `rust/clippy.toml`, `rust/rustfmt.toml`, `rust/deny.toml`, `rust/rust-toolchain.toml`, `android/sdk/gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `ios/sdk/.swift-format`, `ios/sdk/.swiftlint.yml`, `tools/licences.toml` and the root `.editorconfig`. A change to any of those files is a gate change, which its pull request names and whose review checks for weakened rules; the gate fails on a second copy of any listed configuration file, or of a tool configuration that would act like one, anywhere in the tree (AGENTS §10, decision #120): clippy reads `clippy.toml` or `.clippy.toml` and rustfmt `rustfmt.toml` or `.rustfmt.toml` nearest a crate, cargo-deny's `deny.exceptions.toml` and `.deny.exceptions.toml` widen `rust/deny.toml`'s allowlist, ktlint merges every `.editorconfig` up to the root's, Cargo reads a `rust/.cargo/config` in place of `config.toml`, rustup reads the toolchain pin `rust-toolchain.toml` — or the older `rust-toolchain` — from a command's folder and above, so a second copy switches which clippy and rustfmt run (bar the lint library's own pin `rust/never-crash-lints/rust-toolchain.toml`, read only in that folder, which holds no workspace code), and the build's Gradle catalog `libs.versions.toml`, which pins the ktlint and Spotless the Kotlin checks run on, is the one source of every Gradle version (AGENTS §5), so a second copy is a second version set even in `build-logic` (AGENTS §10, decision #133). Tool configurations the gate keeps none of fail it wherever they sit: `.shellcheckrc` and `shellcheckrc`, which shellcheck reads as directives (it also runs with `--norc`), `.ignore` and any `.gitignore` but the root's and `plan/.gitignore`, which jscpd honours (it also runs with `--no-gitignore`), a jscpd ignore marker in the code folders, and a `.sourcekit-lsp` folder, whose configuration SourceKit-LSP merges over the options the Swift stage starts it with. Gradle reads a `gradle.properties` in a project's own folder as that project's properties, so no other `gradle.properties` sits under `android/sdk`: the build's own is `android/sdk/gradle.properties` alone, and `android/sdk/build-logic`, an included build with properties of its own, is where its own may sit (AGENTS §10, decision #122).

**Module build files.** An Android module's build file applies the convention plugin and names its namespace once, and holds only comments, `plugins { id("craftbridge.android.library") }`, `android { namespace = "io.github.christopherlinnett.craftbridge.<module>" }` and a `dependencies` block whose entries are `api`, `implementation`, `testImplementation` or `androidTestImplementation` of a `project(":…")` or a `libs.<alias>`; the root `android/sdk/build.gradle.kts` holds only comments and a `plugins` block of `alias(libs.plugins.<alias>) apply false` lines and `id("craftbridge.quality")`. Every module the settings include has its build file, spelled exactly `build.gradle.kts` because a case-insensitive disk would hand Gradle a `Build.gradle.kts` all the same, no build file is written in Groovy — Gradle would read `build.gradle` in place of `build.gradle.kts`, and the rule reads only Kotlin — and anything else a build needs is configured once in `android/sdk/build-logic`, so a module's file never carries the reach to rewire a check the gate relies on (AGENTS §10, decision #121).
